Whether you need to buy Apple's largest iPhone Pro to get the best camera features varies by generation. So far, most reports have indicated that the cameras on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will not differ, but a leaker today cast some doubt on that claim.

Specifically, they said two features expected to appear on both Pro models 'may' instead be Pro Max exclusives...

The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max had identical camera specs, with all three rear lenses featuring 48-megapixel sensors. Apple said the telephoto lens offers up to 8x optical zoom, but that's achieved by cropping a 24-megapixel image, so the more accurate description is 4x optical zoom with the option to crop to 8x.

So far we have (largely) expected this year's Pro models to maintain matching camera specs, with both getting a variable aperture main lens and a brighter telephoto lens, the latter for better low-light performance.

However, leaker Ice Universe says two new telephoto lens features may be exclusive to the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

If true, that means you'd need to get the Pro Max if you want the longest reach from the telephoto lens and the best low-light performance. However, the word 'may' suggests they're not too sure about this claim, perhaps seeing conflicting evidence in Apple's supply chain.

There has also been some suggestion that the main lens variable aperture system may be a Pro Max exclusive, but reporting on that is mixed.

If you typically prefer the smaller of the two Pro models, would you upgrade to the Pro Max for better camera features? Share your thoughts in the comments.
